quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, ride straight within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the part of your lane that brings you into other drivers' view as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is spotted better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of your lane that brings you into other drivers' view as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane that puts you in an oncoming driver's view as early as possible. For example, when approaching a blind corner on your right, drivers will see you sooner if you ride on the left side of your lane rather than the center.

questions.question: What is a problem with riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes.
It allows you to talk to each other.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. This limits both of your options for escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should passengers do when riding on a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never touch the operator.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Hold onto the seat only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when you turn or go around curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What can help you avoid accidents?

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Look only at your controls, not ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your bike.

questions.question: Should you follow another vehicle differently at night than during the day?

options.text: Yes, allow a longer following distance at night.
No, allow a shorter following distance at night.
No, always use the same following distance.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark because you cannot see shadows and light. Allow a longer following distance when riding at night than you do during the day.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications affect you?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They prevent you from concentrating.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies can make you sleepy and hurt your ability to ride safely. Always know how a medication affects you before you ride.

questions.question: Where should you ride to see better when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, ride in the left portion of your lane. This improves your view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When transporting a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Lean with you.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you when you turn or go around curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control of the motorcycle. They should hold onto handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is considered legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space around you and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Alcohol affects your riding ability:

options.text: Before you reach the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you reach the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Alcohol affects your riding skills even before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following, except:

options.text: Tire air pressure.
Fluid levels.
Turn signals.
Paint damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and turn signals.

questions.question: When riding over a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat so:

options.text: You can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
Your legs can absorb the shock.
Other drivers can see you better.
You can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the shock from the impact. This makes it less likely the impact will throw you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink, then ride:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drunk driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used for quick stops.
Should only be used on slippery roads.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe if used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe if used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, and it is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Secure the load at the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure sidecar loads so they do not shift and change how the motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Downshift.
Speed up.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Gradually apply your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make things worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Avoid braking, as it can worsen the wobble.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals before changing lanes.
Follow other drivers closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, signal your intentions, keep enough space around you, look at least 12 seconds ahead, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.
